title: New tiny blue deep-sea octopus off the Galapagos
verification: Species name, scientist, journal and dates matched across two independent outlets.

slides.headline: Scientists found a tiny blue octopus no one had ever seen before

image.credit: Illustrative photo of a related deep-sea octopus: NOAA National Marine Sanctuaries, public domain

slides.text: It's about the size of a golf ball, and it lives nearly 6,000 feet below the surface off the Galápagos Islands.

image.credit: Photo: David Adam Kess / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.text: A deep-sea camera first filmed it in 2015. The specimen only reached a museum in 2022.
When Field Museum curator Janet Voight finally examined it, her reaction was: "He's tiny! It's blue!"
It's now officially a new species: Microeledone galapagensis, described in the journal Zootaxa.
How many creatures do you think are still hiding down there?

caption:
Scientists have confirmed a brand-new species of octopus living nearly 6,000 feet deep off the Galápagos. It's the size of a golf ball, it's blue, and it took seven years from first sighting to reach a lab.

How many creatures do you think are still hiding down there?

Source: AFP via Dawn
